name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 20 points Republican, among the reddest House seats
Incumbent Riley Moore outraised Ace Parsi roughly six to one
Prediction markets price Moore's win odds near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The seat's roughly 20-point Republican lean, Moore's incumbency and six-to-one fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing his odds near 97 percent all point the same direction. A more favorable national environment for Democrats narrows the expected margin but leaves Parsi a very long underdog.
model.watch: Only a sharp national shift toward Democrats or a major scandal involving Moore would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 20 points toward the GOP. Riley Moore, the incumbent Republican, is seeking another term and holds a large financial edge, having raised about $1.6 million to Democrat Ace Parsi's roughly $277,000. Prediction markets give Moore about a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals. The national political environment appears more favorable to Democrats than in recent cycles, which narrows the expected margin somewhat, but not nearly enough to put the seat in play. Parsi's fundraising, while respectable for a challenger here, leaves him far behind in resources heading into the general election. The race is rated Safe Republican.
